title: List webhooks
summary: List webhook subscriptions. Archived subscriptions are excluded.

response.name: data
response.description: Webhook subscriptions with url, events, and status.

title: Create webhook
summary: Subscribe an http(s) endpoint to one or more session event names and mint its signing secret. The secret is returned by this response only.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Delivery target. Must be an http(s) URL.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: Event names to deliver. At least one is required.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Human-readable label. Defaults to the URL host.

response.name: events
response.description: Subscribed event names. `*` matches every event and a `prefix.*` entry matches that prefix.

response.name: status
response.description: Subscription state. Archived subscriptions are derived from `archived_at` and are excluded from listing and dispatch.

response.name: secret_key
response.description: This subscription's whsec_ signing secret, returned by this response only. Every later read reports the subscription without it.

title: Get webhook
summary: Retrieve a webhook subscription. Archived subscriptions are treated as missing.

title: Update webhook
summary: Update a webhook subscription. Omitted fields keep their stored value.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Delivery target. Must be an http(s) URL when supplied.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: Replacement event name list. Must not be empty.

response.name: events
response.description: Subscribed event names after the update.

title: Archive webhook
summary: Archive a webhook subscription and stop future deliveries.

title: List webhook deliveries
summary: List delivery attempts newest first, including their status codes, retry schedule, and signature.

response.name: data
response.description: Each record carries `status` (`delivered`, `pending_retry`, or `failed`), `status_code`, `error`, `signature`, `attempt_count` (ceiling 3, so at most two retries) and `next_retry_at` (jittered between 5s and a ceiling that doubles from 60s to 120s; `null` once terminal).

title: Send webhook test
summary: Record a signed test delivery without requiring an outbound network call.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Event name for the test payload. Defaults to the first subscribed event.

parameters.name: payload
parameters.description: Overrides merged into the test payload data.

response.name: status
response.description: Test deliveries are recorded as simulated, never sent.

response.name: signature
response.description: `sha256=<hex>` HMAC of the serialized test payload, keyed by this endpoint's signing secret.

title: Dispatch webhook event
summary: Dispatch an event to matching active webhooks and record one delivery per match.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Event name to match against webhook subscriptions.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Event payload delivered to matching webhooks.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Optional caller-supplied event id echoed in the delivered payload.

response.name: data
response.description: One delivery record per matching webhook.

title: Retry due webhook deliveries
summary: Retry failed deliveries whose retry time has arrived, up to fifty per pass.

response.name: data
response.description: Deliveries that were retried in this pass. A retry is another attempt at the same delivery, so it keeps the delivery id and carries the same published header set as the first attempt, re-signed with its own timestamp.

title: Rotate webhook signing secret
summary: Mint a new signing secret and keep the previous one valid, opening a rotation window. Every delivery then carries both signatures in `webhook-signature`, space-separated, so a receiver can migrate without missing a delivery.

response.name: secret_key
response.description: The new whsec_ secret, returned by this response only. The previous secret stays valid until it is retired.

title: Retire previous webhook signing secret
summary: Close the rotation window: the previous secret stops being accepted and only the current one signs. The caller decides when, because only they know when every receiver has moved.
